newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil called up $1.5-2.5, Brent up 10-15 cts.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil called up $1.5-2.5, Brent up 10-15 cts.

text.p: IPE July gas oil was expected to open on Monday up some $1.5-$2.5 a tonne on the back of news over the weekend that Iraqi crude exports are not expected to restart until August and on the back of Friday's strong crude close, brokers said.

Iraq's key negotiator for a U.N. oil-for-food deal said on Saturday that Baghdad was ready to resume oil sales in August under the second round of the accord approved this month if New York did not delay agreement.

If all went smoothly, Abdul Amir al-Anbari said: "End of July, beginning of August we would resume our oil discussions. We'll have to sign contracts and they have to be approved by the oil experts in New York."
July gas oil rose $2 on the Friday to close at $163.75 a tonne.
August IPE Brent crude settled on Friday up 33 cents at $18.18 but was set to make further gains on the back of the weekend news, brokers said.
They saw the prompt contract gaining a further 10-15 cents on the opening on Monday. The first resistance the contract would hit was almost 30 cents above Friday's settle at $18.45 a barrel.
"It shouldn't have any problems making the call. The crude markets over here are tight and this (Iraq) news helps the push upwards," one said.
Resistance at $18.45 for the prompt contract was not only last Wednesday's high but the top of a rally from $17.49 a barrel.
Brokers were not sure whether the markets would see further fund buying this week. Strong buying on Friday from financial funds who had shorted the market helped the upward move.
Brent on SIMEX was untraded with the bid/ask ranges wide apart. On the August a bid of $18.25 met an offer some 14 cents higher.
